subject: koala
pitch: A sleepy koala hugging a eucalyptus branch. Soft ash-grey fur with a cream chest and cream-lined fluffy ears, a big black leathery nose, half-closed drowsy brown eyes, strong grey paws with dark claws, and a sprig of blue-green eucalyptus leaves in one hand, mid-munch.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a koala design facing forward, sitting and hugging a eucalyptus branch, trying to decide whether the branch should sit horizontally in front of its chest or in some other orientation to make the pose read clearly.

I'm sketching the skeleton structure: hip root, spine to chest, neck and head with jaw, arms with shoulder-elbow-wrist-finger chains, and legs with hip-knee-ankle joints, while working out proportions for a roughly 0.65m sitting koala and setting coordinates for the perch branch and base.

Now I'm detailing the body geometry -- scaled ellipsoid spheres for the lower body, chest, and wide head, plus rounded ears with cream inner fluff, a small black nose with sheen, and drowsy dark eyes topped with grey eyelid caps for a sleepy look.

I'm adding a separate lower jaw box at the joint and positioning a leaf sprig held up near the koala's mouth by its left hand.

Now I'm sketching a hugged branch diagonally across the chest, with the right arm wrapping over it and the left hand gripping near the top where the leafy tip extends.

I'm placing the right wrist along the branch curve so the paw wraps around it, with small curled finger capsules and dark claws over the top. For the arms I'll build smooth sweeps along shoulder-elbow-wrist chains rather than rigid cylinders, keeping the limbs simple before moving to the legs.

Now I'm working out the hip-knee-ankle positions so the thighs rest against the branch and the feet grip the perch from the front, adjusting the foot placement slightly to sit naturally over the curved surface. I'm defining the perch itself as a cylinder along the X-axis with a small radius, so the figure's feet and body can sit properly on top of it.

The perch needs a flat resting point since it's essentially a log lying on the ground, so I'm giving it brown bark with grain painting, a few stubs, and a knot for texture. For the leaves, I'm deciding to extrude a lanceolate leaf outline into a thin shape rather than deform a sphere, sketching out the leaf's point coordinates to form a tapered, pointed shape.

Thinking more about eucalyptus foliage, those adult leaves are long and sickle-shaped, so I'll extrude along x and y directions with smoothing applied. I'm working out the rig now too: attaching leaves to a "branch" joint under the chest rather than directly to hand joints, then building the skeleton hierarchy from hips up through spine, chest, and neck.

Continuing the joint setup, I need a root joint before chaining the spine since boneFor and weightsFor will throw errors without one. Building out the spine chain with hips, spine, and chest knots, then moving on to the neck and head chain anchored at the chest tip.

Now I'm planning the head, jaw and body construction: head and jaw joints parented under neck with appropriate hinge directions, then building body parts from spheres scaled to the bones, and setting up fur coloring with countershading (grey back, cream belly) and mottled texture patterns.

Still placing ear details...

Now I'm placing the nose as a big black scaled sphere near the top of the muzzle bulge, adding a tiny lighter highlight sphere for the nostril shine, and planning a thin mouth line beneath it.

I'm working out the lower jaw geometry—sizing a cream-colored box for the jaw joint positioned just under the muzzle, and setting the head sphere's center and radius so the eyes can be placed symmetrically on its surface using the sphere equation to find the correct depth at each eye's x-offset.

Now I'm figuring out eyelid details: giving the eye a dark brown iris, adding a grey upper eyelid hemisphere slightly squashed over it, and considering a thin dark line or box to suggest the lower lid edge where the hemisphere's flat bottom meets the eye center.

For the hands, I'm shaping paws into flattened spheres at the wrist with three small capsule fingers curling around the branch, working out wrist positions and branch parameter values so the grip looks natural along the branch's angle.

Still working out finger geometry...

Spacing fingers across that arc, then placing the wrist endpoint and claw cone at the last angle, computing the actual coordinates for both the right branch contact point and left branch contact point to anchor each hand.

I'm bending the branch upward so it curves toward the mouth, adjusting the end segment so leaves cluster near the mouth position while staying just in front of the nose depth.

Writing leaf extrusion function...

I'm planning around 14 leaves along the branch using blue-green tones, with droopy varied directions and sickle-shaped outlines. For the legs, I'm setting up thigh thickness and joint chains for hip, knee, and ankle, deciding how many points each chain needs.

Now I'm defining the leg sweep radii tapering from thicker hip to thinner ankle, then setting up the arm chains parented to the chest joint with shoulder-elbow-wrist points and matching tapered radii. I'm also working out the paw at the ankle with scaled spheres and three curling toes with claws positioned near the perch.

Still sizing body parts...

Now I'm setting up the bone hierarchy with a root at the hips and a spine chain, then planning the fur paint colors using a mottled pattern.

I'm adding wool tufts for the ears, head, and cheeks using small cream and grey spheres and cones, then defining the perch as a swept cylinder bound to the root bone with flat caps and a grain-colored texture.

Now I'm adding lighter end discs to the perch caps, plus a small branch stub with leaves, and starting a bark-colored branch using a catmull curve sweep with tapering radii.

I'm defining colors for claws and eyes, then setting up a shared hand-wrapping function that computes perpendicular basis vectors so I can mirror the grip pose between left and right hands.

Working out the paw placement next, defining a wristPoint function so the finger sweep endpoint lines up with where the wrist bone terminates, then tracing the arm chain from shoulder to elbow to wrist with actual coordinates for each joint.

I'm now building a reusable foot/toe helper that positions the ankle, places a flattened sphere for the foot pad, and sweeps three small capsules outward and downward from the foot for the toes.

The toe tips were overshooting past the perch's front edge, looking like paws dangling in midair, so I'm adjusting the ankle's z-position onto the perch top and curling the toe capsule path inward so the tips land closer to the perch's front edge instead of hanging off it.

Working out the leg chain positions for hip, knee, and ankle so the shin and thigh proportions stay anatomically plausible while sitting on the perch — hip and butt overlapping slightly at the back is fine since it's hidden by the body mass.

Now I'm working out the ear geometry: positioning each ear center outward from the head, rotating it around the vertical axis so it angles outward and forward, with an inner cream-colored patch offset and rotated to match, plus small rim tufts spaced around the ear's edge while skipping the ones near the bottom. Then I'm placing a thin dark philtrum line under the nose on the head's front face.

Next I'm figuring out the muzzle bump, nose, and philtrum placements by calculating how far the curved head surface projects forward at each height, then positioning a muzzle sphere, a protruding nose shape, and a small philtrum box so they sit correctly on that curve. I'm also adding two slightly angled boxes for the mouth line and a jaw block beneath the muzzle, using the same surface-distance math to keep everything flush against the head.

Now I'm setting up the jaw joint and rigging, parenting eyes and mouth details to the head bone, then moving into the leaf generation logic—defining a sickle-shaped leaf outline, extruding it along branch directions with randomized scale and color, and sizing leaves to roughly eucalyptus proportions.

I'm placing leaves along the branch curve using tangent-based directions, clustering extra leaves near the tip with fanned, droopy orientations, and adding a short perch stub with its own small leaf cluster near the character's mouth.

Now I'm setting up geometry shortcuts like a sphere-ball helper for building body parts, and defining the fur/mottle texture painting per bone (head, torso, hips), along with the spine chain names and path points for the skeleton.

Next I'm wiring up the joint hierarchy -- root, neck/head chain, jaw joint, a branch joint off the chest, and then the arm chains with left/right naming conventions, looping over sides to mirror the limb joints.

For the fur sweep, I'm defining a tapering radius array along the chain and checking that the perch's bottom sits exactly at ground level before writing the final code.
